chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Abbas from Aban from al-Halabi Ubayd Allah said:

A boy moved a basket and broke two eggs in the Haram (sanctuary). I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he said: 'Two Jaddayn or two Hamalayn.' This is not contradictory to what we said earlier, because this report is understood to mean that if the egg is one in which the chick has already moved, then at that time a ransom of one Hamal or one Jaddayn is obligatory upon him. And if there was no movement of the chick in it, then its value (Qimah) is due upon him, according to what we presented earlier, which indicates that.

key_terms.الْإِحْرَامُ: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.جَدَيٌّ: A specific measure of eggs (usually two dozen)
key_terms.حَمَلٌ: A specific measure of eggs (usually one dozen)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for breaking pigeon eggs in the Haram while in Ihram?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq) to clarify the distinction between fixed ransom (Jaddayn/Hamal) and actual value (Qimah) based on embryonic movement. This hadith establishes the jurisprudential principle that the liability for breaking pigeon eggs in the Haram during Ihram is determined by the developmental stage of the embryo, distinguishing between a moving fetus and a static egg.
